balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Align Technology, Inc.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Align Technology, Inc.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Align Technology, Inc.: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Align Technology, Inc.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Align: with no debt and over $1.1bn of cash, FCF is funding an expanded buyback (raised to $400-500m for FY2026 after Elliott's activist stake) rather than deleveraging -- so a dip in FCF shows up in slower repurchases, not balance-sheet stress.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • CapEx step-up as the ~$200m Hyderabad, India plant (2027) ramps

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Align: gross margin benefits from the mix shift toward higher-margin Clear Aligner revenue and away from lower-margin scanner hardware, but GAAP operating margin is currently depressed by 2026 restructuring charges (~$35-37m) and legal settlements (the $32m Misty Snow antitrust payment, the ~$43m UK VAT accrual). Q4 2026 guide is ~26% non-GAAP vs ~20% GAAP operating margin -- that gap is almost entirely these one-offs.

What to watch:

  • GAAP vs non-GAAP operating margin converging once restructuring/legal charges roll off
  • Gross margin eroding if price competition from Straumann/Angelalign forces discounting

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Align Technology, Inc.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Align: net income has stayed close to operating income because the balance sheet carries no debt, so there is little interest expense pulling the two apart -- interest *income* on cash is the main item between them.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep, restructuring charges)
  • Net income far from operating income (legal settlements, tax items)

caseShipments.title: Case shipments: total vs teen
caseShipments.content:
Case shipments are Invisalign clear-aligner cases shipped to doctors in the period (thousands); teen case shipments are the subset for teenage patients, a segment Align has targeted with dedicated products (e.g. features for growing teeth, compliance indicators).

For Align: Q3 2026 case shipments were a record for the company and North America orthodontist shipments rose YoY for the first time in six quarters -- the key open question is whether that holds into Q4 and 2027, against four prior years of declining orthodontic case starts.

What to watch:

  • Whether total case growth is coming from international volume or a genuine North America recovery
  • Teen share of shipments, a proxy for how much growth is discretionary adult demand vs the more stable teen channel

doctorUtilization.title: Doctor submitters and utilization rate
doctorUtilization.content:
Doctor submitters are the number of Invisalign-trained doctors (thousands) who submitted at least one case and received a shipment in the period. Utilization rate is case shipments divided by doctor submitters -- cases per doctor, Align's own disclosed metric.

For Align: doctor submitters hit a record 90.9 thousand in Q3 2026 (+3.1% YoY) and utilization rate rose to 7.6 cases per doctor from 7.3 -- so volume growth is coming from both a wider doctor base (GP channel penetration) and doctors submitting more cases each, not just one or the other.

What to watch:

  • Utilization rate falling even as submitter count rises (dilution from newly onboarded, lower-volume doctors)
  • GP dentist additions versus orthodontist additions -- the GP channel is the stated growth lever

revenuePerCase.title: Clear Aligner revenue per case
revenuePerCase.content:
Revenue per case is Clear Aligner segment revenue divided by case shipments -- the average selling price per treatment, as Align itself discloses it.

For Align: revenue per case has been drifting down (e.g. $1,245 in Q3 2025 to $1,215 in Q3 2026, -2.4%) as case-volume growth outpaces revenue growth. That is consistent with margin-steering by lower-priced competitors (Straumann/Smartee, Angelalign) and a mix shift toward lower-priced configurations such as the Doctor Subscription Program.

What to watch:

  • ASP decline accelerating, which would point to real price competition rather than mix
  • Whether volume growth is big enough to offset ASP erosion in segment revenue

segmentRevenue.title: Segment revenue
segmentRevenue.content:
Align reports two segments: Clear Aligner (Invisalign aligners, Vivera retainers; ~82% of revenue) and Systems & Services (iTero scanners, CAD/CAM software, exocad; ~18%).

For Align: Clear Aligner keeps growing on international case volume while Systems & Services has declined for multiple consecutive quarters (-7.6% YoY in Q3 2026) on weak capital-equipment demand and a mix shift to lower-priced/leased scanners -- FY2026 guidance for the segment was cut again in October 2026 to ~$715-725m.

What to watch:

  • Systems & Services decline rate stabilizing versus deepening
  • Clear Aligner growth rate versus total company guidance

segmentOperatingIncome.title: Segment operating income
segmentOperatingIncome.content:
Operating income by segment -- how much of each segment's revenue converts to operating profit, before corporate overhead allocation differences are netted out in consolidation.

For Align: Clear Aligner carries the clear majority of segment operating income and its margin is the one management can still grow (through mix and pricing); Systems & Services' shrinking revenue base makes its operating income more exposed to fixed-cost deleverage as volumes fall.

What to watch:

  • Systems & Services operating income falling faster than its revenue (deleverage)
  • Clear Aligner operating margin trend as the main driver of consolidated operating margin expansion the company has guided toward for FY2027

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Align: revenue has been roughly flat at $3.7-4.1bn for five years because Clear Aligner growth (international case volume) has been largely offset by a declining Systems & Services segment and soft North American demand -- FY2026 guidance was cut to $4.11-4.13bn in October 2026. Watch whether Q3 2026's first North America shipment uptick in six quarters is a turn or a blip.

What to watch:

  • Whether international case growth keeps outrunning the North America slowdown
  • Systems & Services continuing to shrink against Clear Aligner growth
  • Interim rows show seasonality (orthodontic case starts dip in H2)

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Align Technology, Inc.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
